findings.pixel_evidence: Two fracture pieces are visible. Both have broadly similar large round holes; remaining tray contents are assorted unrelated-shaped hardware, so no same-scale unmodified versus enlarged sample-hole comparison can be read. Surface wear is generic mottling; a specific dismantling trace is not independently distinguishable. A drill alone does not demonstrate either physical fact.
findings.missing_visual_information: A comparable baseline hole, visibly enlarged counterpart, and localized reassembly/tool-contact traces tied to the same examined clasp; these are inspectable clue facts, not decorative variants.
findings.bounded_output: One focused original medieval pixel-art evidence close-up on an opaque neutral background. Three clearly separated inspection groups: two complementary fragments of ONE clasp laid at a small gap with stable fracture outline; ONE intact same-design same-scale control sample beside its corresponding enlarged-hole fragment with visibly distinguishable bore rims; and enlarged view of localized opposing tool-contact/scuffed fastener-seat traces on that SAME broken clasp. Keep the drill beside the sample as scale/reference, not touching or drilling. Finite samples, no people or labels, no inferred material fault, ethnicity, automatic guilt, completed testing or compensation. Exact wear shape is art proposal. If the three views cannot keep object identity clear, generate a single larger two-sample comparison plus a small inset of the same fastener seat.
findings.duplication_check: All current registered asset prompts searched. No later corrective inspection close-up found; early09 remains selected. Environment08 and action10 do not replace readable physical clue comparison.
